AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Hip pain in young and middle- aged adults with and without hip deformity receive treatment focused primarily related to hip structure. Because their hip pain may be chronic, these patients develop other modifiable co-existing disorders related to pain that go undiagnosed in this young and active population including insomnia and anxiety.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The objective is to compare assessments of insomnia and anxiety in young and middle-aged adults presenting with hip pain with no greater than minimal osteoarthritis (OA) compared to asymptomatic (healthy) controls.Comparisons between types of hip deformity and no hip deformity in hip pain patients were performed to assess if patients with specific hip deformities were likely to have insomnia or anxiety as a cofounding disorder to their hip pain.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Prospective case series with control comparison.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Two tertiary university physiatry outpatient clinics.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Fifty hip pain patients aged 18-40 years and 50 gender and aged matched healthy controls.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Patients were enrolled if: 2 provocative hip tests were found on physical examination and hip radiographs had no or minimal OA. Radiographic hip deformity measurements were completed by an independent examiners. Comparisons of insomnia and anxiety were completed between: 1) 50 hip pain patients and 50 controls and 2) patients with different types of hip deformity.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Insomnia severity Index (ISI) and Pain anxiety Symptom Scale (PASS) RESULTS: Fifty hip pain patients (11 male, 39 female) with mean age of 31.2+8.31 years enrolled. Hip pain patients slept significantly less (p=.001) per night than controls. Patients experienced significantly greater insomnia (p=.0001) and anxiety (p=.0001) compared to controls. No differences were found in insomnia and anxiety scores between hip pain patients with and without hip deformity or between types of hip deformity.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Hip pain patients with radiographs demonstrating minimal to no hip arthritis with and without hip deformity experience significant cofounding yet modifiable disorders of sleep and anxiety. If recognized early in presentation, treatment of insomnia and anxiety ultimately will improve outcomes for hip patients treated conservatively or surgically for their hip disorder.
